item.title: The cost of operating amid debris
item.description: Multiple in-orbit servicing ventures have emerged to tackle the industry’s rising debris risk, but finding paying customers remains a core challenge even as government-backed demos ramp up and key technologies are proven in orbit.

item.title: Space is a warfighting domain. Our industrial base must reflect that.
item.description: When I served as acting Secretary of Defense, I took a trip to Buckley Space Force Base. I went as someone who understood in the abstract that space had become contested. I left understanding it in my gut. Watching the men and women who track every object on orbit and leverage space-based sensors to spot a launch anywhere on Earth to give our ground forces the seconds of warning that save lives, I came away with a conviction that has only deepened since: Space is a warfighting domain, and we are not yet organized to win in it.

item.description: Astrolab, a company developing crewed and robotic rovers, is expanding into lunar infrastructure with systems that can provide power and communications for a future moon base.

item.title: Satellite on orbit responded to voice command in experimental first
item.description: Operators on the ground successfully directed a satellite on orbit with a voice command for the first time. Researchers told SpaceNews that their experimental success could be a step toward a future in which responsive satellites can listen for distress calls and emergency signals from ships at sea.

item.title: The 2028 Imperative: NASA’s 2028 crunch for Artemis, SR-1 and robotic lunar landings
item.description: During his first few months as NASA administrator, Jared Isaacman shook up many of the agency’s key programs. In February, he announced that Artemis 3 — expected to be the first crewed landing attempt on the moon since 1972 — would instead be a test flight in low Earth orbit involving Orion and two lunar landers in mid-2027. It would, though, set up two landing attempts on the moon in 2028 on Artemis 4 and 5.

item.title: Hydrosat announces new thermal imaging program for European defense customers
item.description: JOHANNESBURG — Thermal imaging company Hydrosat announced a new high-resolution midwave infrared imaging program that will provide tactical intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance capabilities for European governments and allied defense customers.

item.title: Europe looks beyond the ISS
item.description: European Space Agency member states will meet in Rome Dec. 15 to decide the future of Europe’s human and robotic exploration program. The meeting breaks with ESA’s usual three-year ministerial cycle, giving ministers an earlier opportunity to respond to the approaching end of the ISS and growing calls for Europe to secure a more autonomous role in human spaceflight and exploration.
